description: Season-to-date for one resort from PeakCam's own daily station record: measured snowfall since the season start (daily new snow = the positive change in station depth, a floor on what fell), days measured, snow days, powder days (8 in or more, the alert threshold), current and deepest base, percent of the 30-winter normal to this day and of the recent decade (with a baselineNote when they disagree by more than 10 %), the same day last year, a 7-day trend and a dated sentence to quote. Use it for "how is the season going", "is this a good year", "how does it compare with last year".

slug.description: PeakCam resort slug, lowercase kebab-case, e.g. `breckenridge`. Get it from search_resorts.

name: get_season_stats

asOf.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the newest daily reading this season.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD the depth was first reached.

diffIn.description: This season minus last season, inches.

key.description: Water year for the Northern hemisphere (Oct 2026 → 2027); calendar year for the Southern.

startDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD the season starts: Oct 1 (North) or Apr 1 (South).

seasonToDateIn.description: Cumulative snowfall by the same day of season last year.

baselineNote.description: Set when the two baselines differ by more than 10 %; quote it with the percent.

recentDecade.description: The same against the 10 most recent winters.

thirtyYear.description: Season-to-date snowfall as a percent of the 30-winter mean by this day; null without a normal.

key.description: Water year for the Northern hemisphere (Oct 2026 → 2027); calendar year for the Southern.

startDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD the season starts: Oct 1 (North) or Apr 1 (South).

sentence.description: A dated sentence that can be quoted verbatim.

anyOf.description: `snotel`: daily NRCS station readings, quality-controlled. `open_meteo`: weather-model daily values for resorts without a station.

elevationFt.description: Station elevation in feet. Measurements describe this elevation, not the resort's summit.

title: Season stats
